sources.source: Apache Spark 3.5.9 Documentation, "Performance Tuning" (Adaptive Query Execution)

items.item: AQE enabled by default since Spark 3.2.0; three major features since Spark 3.0: coalescing post-shuffle partitions, converting sort-merge join to broadcast join, skew join optimization

at.step: Reveal: re-optimization happens at stage boundaries

items.item: Coalescing simplifies tuning the shuffle-partition count by picking it from real map-output statistics at runtime

at.step: Reveal: coalescing shuffle partitions

items.item: A partition is skewed if its size exceeds a factor times the median partition size, and also exceeds an absolute byte threshold; splits (and replicates) it into roughly even pieces

at.step: How a skewed partition gets found and split

items.item: Trino collects candidate join-condition values from the build side and pushes a runtime predicate (reported in queryStats as a SortedRangeSet, a min/max-style range) into the probe-side scan

at.step: Reveal: dynamic partition pruning

items.item: For a partitioned source (the Hive connector), this is explicitly named "dynamic partition pruning" by Trino's own docs

at.step: Reveal: dynamic partition pruning

items.item: Partition pruning happens not only at planning time but also during execution, for parameter values unknown at plan time (PREPARE parameters, subquery values, parameterized nested-loop joins)

at.step: How PostgreSQL prunes partitions at execution time

items.item: The number of partitions removed at plan-initialization time is reported via the "Subplans Removed" EXPLAIN property

at.step: How PostgreSQL prunes partitions at execution time

Reveal: splitting needs spare capacity to pay off

items.item: The specific reason skew-splitting needs spare executor slots to pay off (the total work is unchanged; only idle capacity turns a split into a real wall-clock win), not just asserted but reasoned from the measured non-result

Why a local, single-process Trino or Spark-cluster run couldn't honestly demonstrate dynamic partition pruning's own benefit (it is a cross-node, network-avoidance claim, not a single-job statistics claim like coalescing or skew-splitting), disclosed rather than silently skipped

items.item: The precise distinction between a runtime filter (row-level, from a join condition) and dynamic partition pruning (the same mechanism applied at partition/file granularity) — not conflated as the same thing

at.step: Reveal: dynamic partition pruning

items.item: A genuine, locally reproduced PostgreSQL execution-time partition-pruning result (Subplans Removed: 3, ~3.2x faster, 4x fewer buffer reads), requiring the `force_generic_plan` trick to actually observe (a literal parameter value would otherwise let the planner prune at plan time, hiding the execution-time mechanism)

items.item: "Sideways information passing" read precisely as one side of a join passing real values to the other side's scan, not down a fixed plan tree — the structural reason the syllabus groups runtime filters and dynamic partition pruning together

items.item: The structural link back to topic 25: the broadcast threshold there was a plan-time constant; this topic shows the same decision revisited at runtime once real sizes are known, the same way partition-wise joins (topic 25) and partition pruning (this topic) are both single-machine analogs of a cluster-scale idea
